title: Quantum Correlations and the Tsirelson Bound in a Physical–Observation Dual-Axis Structure—From the Physobser Axiom and U(1) Phase Transport to CP1, the Born Pairing, and Bell Correlations
content: For finite-dimensional binary systems and their bipartite composites, this paper establishes a conditional representation chain from a physical–observation dual-axis structure to quantum Bell correlations. An observational fact is jointly generated by a complete physical state and a complete observation state. Additivity and associativity of coherent responses, two-sided cancellation, and a full circle group of scalar phase transport select C among finite-dimensional unital associative real response algebras. Reversible mixing then determines a Hermitian metric up to an overall positive factor. Normalized two-channel responses form \(S^3\), and quotienting by their common phase yields the rank-one observation-event space and, with an outcome label, the pure observation fiber \(S^3/U(1)=CP^1≃S^2\). The universal bilinear composite of two independent systems is \(C^4\). Probabilities are first assigned within complete measurement contexts. Events with the same response filter are operationally interchangeable, so the local assignments glue along the observation axis into a positive orthogonally additive measure on the full projection lattice. Gleason's theorem then gives the unique trace representation \(p(P∣x)=Tr(ρ_xP)\), while composite marginal consistency returns the trace pairing to each local binary fiber. Every two-qubit correlation therefore has the universal form \(E_ρ(a,b)=a^TT_ρb\). Joint rotational invariance and perfect equal-axis anticorrelation uniquely fix \(T_ρ=−I_3\), producing the singlet cosine law E=−a⋅b=−cos⁡θ. Finally, the local commutators in the squared CHSH operator confine all realizable correlations to \(2\sqrt{2}\). Fine-measurement completeness supplies saturating directions, while sharp preparation and reversible covariance make the singlet accessible. Thus \(CP^1\), the Born pairing, the cosine correlation law, and the Tsirelson bound arise within one chain linking phase structure, independent composition, and cross-context probability consistency.
